name: Lash tint

lead: Lash tinting darkens eyelashes with dye so they look fuller and the eyes more defined without mascara. It is a common salon service, and the colour holds for several weeks.
Wikipedia lists tints alongside extensions among popular salon eyelash procedures. No published clinical studies of lash tinting were identified.

paras: A dye is applied to the lashes in a salon and stains the hair itself, so the colour lasts until the lashes shed. Users book repeat visits to maintain it and skip mascara day to day.

In the United States the FDA says hair dyes should not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows and that no color additives are approved for that use, citing reports of eye injuries, including blindness, from dyes used near the eyes.

angle.text: Lash tinting dyes the lashes darker so they look fuller and the eyes look more defined without mascara, a visible change that lasts several weeks. It is a common salon service. The effect is cosmetic and directly observable.

lead: Lash tinting is a salon procedure in which a dye is applied to eyelashes to darken them, so they look fuller without mascara. Wikipedia lists tints, alongside extensions, among popular salon eyelash procedures.[1]

In the United States, the FDA states that hair dyes should not be used on eyebrows or eyelashes, and that no color additives are approved for dyeing them. The agency cites reports of eye injuries, including blindness, from hair dyes used near the eyes.[2]
No published clinical studies of lash tinting were identified, and little other source material is available.
infobox: FDA: no color additives approved for eyelash dyeing[2]

paras: The FDA advises that hair dyes not be used on eyebrows or eyelashes and says coal-tar hair dyes are not approved for that use. A color additive intended for lashes or brows would need FDA approval for that specific use.[2]
